correctness.rationale: For every positive wet-decay and dry-recovery parameter, the two wet flow integrals and affine dry recovery map compose exactly to normalized excess uptake \(2-b-bac-(1-b)(a+c)\). At a fixed positive gap, strict AM–GM gives the unique equal wet split. Differentiation of the resulting objective gives \(G_T'(\delta)=A[-\eta-z+bB(z)]\) and \(G_T''(\delta)=-A[(kz/2)(1-bB_z)+hbB]\), with \(B=z(1-z)+r(1-z)^2\) and \(B_z=1-2z-2r(1-z)<1\). Thus strict concavity and the negative terminal-gap derivative are global. At zero gap the derivative is \(A[r(1-z)^2-z^2-\eta]\), which rises strictly with the horizon and crosses zero once exactly when \(r>\eta\), giving the explicit critical horizon. Positive horizon derivative and negative gap derivative of the first-order condition establish monotone optimal rest; that equation bounds the rest above by \(h^{-1}\log(r/\eta)\) and identifies its limit. The implicit function theorem gives the linear onset coefficient. A standalone reproducible standard-library program checks 3,000 parameter cases, separate quadrature, derivatives, an exact logarithmic benchmark and asymptotics. Universal assertions rest on the displayed inequalities, not the random tests.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General optimal-control and pulse-sequencing techniques may encompass finite switching problems, but generic existence principles, numerical optimizers and standard Pontryagin switching conditions alone do not state the explicit global fixed-horizon threshold, unique optimizer, saturation formula or onset coefficient. Karmeli–Peri describes pulse-design parameters for several cycles; Dadhich considers time to apply a prescribed dose. No inspected broader source provides a result that implies this entire theorem without a new analysis. Residual specialized coverage remains possible.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Gençoğlan et al. determine ponding times and numbers/lengths of on cycles to meet a specified water depth, without analyzing an independently selectable dry recovery gap at fixed terminal clock time. The OpenSWMM documentation gives wet and dry state equations but no optimization theorem. Assouline derives single-event rate/duration relationships to prevent runoff, not capacity-saturated recovery scheduling. Dadhich treats cycle time saving for fixed dose: overlap cannot be decisively excluded without full text but its stated optimization differs. An earlier Green–Ampt temporal rearrangement theorem compares equimeasurable rainfall patterns with cumulative infiltration state and no drying regeneration, so neither its state equation nor its dominance ordering implies the present rest-threshold result. This implication comparison is about domains, objective functions and quantifiers, not matching titles.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: In the equivalent switched-affine-state formulation, wet excess capacity is multiplied by an exponential decay while dry recovery is an exponential affine map; the objective is the integral of capacity on exactly two wet intervals. A pulse-irrigation model with a fixed dose, fixed rainfall level below capacity, no recovery state, or arbitrarily many cycles does not imply the asserted unique one-gap horizon policy. The inspected published material gives the individual flows, ponding-time estimates or single-event dose/rate design, but does not state the joint concavity and critical horizon. Such equivalences were searched at the statement and state-space level.

originality.rationale: The originality claim is limited to the complete fixed-horizon, one-gap, two-pulse capacity-recovery classification: unique equal wet splits for any positive gap, global strict gap concavity, exact necessary-and-sufficient horizon threshold, increasing finite-saturating optimal rest and sharp linear onset. Wet Horton decay, dry exponential recovery, and intermittent sprinkler operation are prior art. Full primary material inspected for Gençoğlan et al. (2005) and Assouline (2019) addresses ponding/cycle counts and fixed-dose rate design rather than this freely optimized fixed-clock recovery gap. Accessible excerpts of Dadhich et al. (2012), Karmeli–Peri (1974) and James–Larson (1976) have other stated objectives, but uninspected full texts and broader optimal-control theorems leave acknowledged priority risk. Actual mathematical-record searches yielded no theorem covering the joint conclusion; absent results are not treated as uniqueness proof.

value.rationale: The natural resource-allocation decision trades recovery of infiltration capacity against wet exposure lost during the hiatus. Optimizing both wet durations and the single gap under a terminal horizon gives an exact criterion \(hA>kf_c\) for whether a beneficial gap can ever exist, a separate sharp horizon threshold for when it does, global uniqueness, an explicit finite long-horizon rest cap and linear critical response. These address structurally meaningful questions in a standard hydrology approximation, supplying benchmarks for numerical pulsed-irrigation models. The value does not depend on a new general control theorem or experimental validation; the restricted two-pulse regime and nonimplication for multicycle schedules are explicit.
